answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions behind a time-locked stake that is slashed when bonded agents are caught coordinating fraud. For example, a raven agent may submit a claim, while a vertex of independent reviewers checks it against signed, randomly assigned evidence; an opal reward is released only after agreement. Creating many identities does not create more influence, because each must lock scarce capital and pass the same checks. A sybil operator risks losing that stake and paying the opportunity cost of keeping it locked.
